Tenant acme then gets https://github.com/acme/acme-gitops. A tenant can also override its own repositories by annotation — see Reference.

docs.title: 2. Opt the tenant in
docs.text:
kubectl annotate tenant acme argocd.tenantoperator.stakater.com/enabled=true
kubectl -n multi-tenant-operator wait \
  templateinstances.templates.v2.stakater.com/mto-argocd-tenant-acme \
  --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Ready --timeout=90s

docs.title: 3. See the AppProject
docs.text:
kubectl -n openshift-gitops get appproject acme -o yaml

The project is scoped to the tenant's namespaces, with three roles bound to its groups and users:

spec:
  description: Managed by mto-extension-argocd
  sourceRepos:
    - https://github.com/acme/acme-gitops
  destinations:                       # the tenant's namespaces, never the ArgoCD namespace
    - { namespace: acme-dev,  server: https://kubernetes.default.svc }
    - { namespace: acme-prod, server: https://kubernetes.default.svc }
  roles:
    - name: acme-owner
      groups:
        - acme-owner-group-c2ef09     # the MTO-generated group (OpenShift)
        - acme-admins                 # the tenant's groups
        - alice@acme.example          # and its users — see Security
      policies:
        - p, proj:acme:acme-owner, applications, *, acme/*, allow
        - p, proj:acme:acme-owner, applicationsets, *, acme/*, allow
        # ... repositories, clusters, logs
    # acme-edit: get, sync, update on applications; get on the rest
    # acme-view: get on everything

docs.title: 4. Deploy an Application
docs.text:
The tenant's owners and editors can now create Applications in that project. By default Applications live in the ArgoCD namespace; to let tenants keep them in their own namespaces instead, see Applications in tenant namespaces.

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: acme-web
  namespace: openshift-gitops
spec:
  project: acme
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/acme/acme-gitops
    path: web
    targetRevision: main
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: acme-dev

ArgoCD accepts it because the repo matches sourceRepos and the destination is one of the project's destinations. A destination outside the tenant's namespaces, or a repo outside its sourceRepos, is refused.

What this looks like to a tenant's developers

Tenant members do nothing to set this up. They sign in to ArgoCD with their usual identity, and their group gives them owner, edit or view in their own project — they see and manage only their own Applications. An owner or editor creates Applications (in the ArgoCD UI/API, or by kubectl apply once Applications in tenant namespaces is enabled); edit cannot delete or override, and view is read-only. They never touch an AppProject or ArgoCD RBAC.

docs.title: What a tenant cannot do
docs.text:
• Deploy into a namespace it does not own — destinations is the tenant's namespaces only.
  • Deploy into the ArgoCD control-plane namespace — never a destination (see Security).
  • Deploy from a repository outside its sourceRepos.
  • Manage a cluster-scoped kind unless the platform allow-listed it (see Reference).

Previous: Installation · Next: Applications in tenant namespaces

docs.title: Identity and sync impersonation
docs.text:
Two independent settings: how the project's roles name their groups, and whose identity a sync runs as.

Setting Chart value Default Effect Groups named by pattern identity.mode accessControl roles use the Tenant's groups/users; groupPattern or both uses IdP groups named tenant-<t>-<tier> Sync impersonation argocd.impersonation.enabled false syncs run as a ServiceAccount in the destination namespace instead of the cluster-admin controller

docs.title: Groups named by pattern
docs.text:
By default (identity.mode: accessControl) each role's groups are the Tenant's owners, editors and viewers, plus the MTO-generated group and any privileged groups. The other Stakater extensions instead take access from identity-provider groups named by a pattern, and so can this one:

identity:
  mode: groupPattern                              # or 'both' while moving over
  groupPattern: "tenant-{{ tenant }}-{{ tier }}"  # the default

Tenant acme then gets tenant-acme-owners, tenant-acme-editors and tenant-acme-viewers. The MTO-generated and privileged groups are kept in every mode; both appends the pattern groups to the Tenant's own lists.

This matters most on OpenShift with external OIDC (4.20+), where the MTO-generated OpenShift group never reaches ArgoCD, and wherever user entries would otherwise need scopes: [groups, email] (see Security). The pattern must contain both {{ tenant }} and {{ tier }}. Use a prefix your identity provider controls, and never a name a local ArgoCD user has — an SSO group named like a local user inherits that user's roles.

docs.title: Sync impersonation
docs.text:
Off by default. Without it, every sync runs as ArgoCD's application controller, which upstream ships with a */*/* ClusterRole — so a sync can do anything, anywhere. With it, ArgoCD syncs as a ServiceAccount in the destination namespace, and a sync can only do what the tenant could do itself:

argocd:
  impersonation:
    enabled: true
    serviceAccount: argocd-deployer   # the default

Every AppProject then carries one destinationServiceAccounts entry per tenant namespace, with defaultServiceAccount: argocd-deployer. There is deliberately no catch-all entry, unlike the upstream example: a destination without an entry fails the sync rather than falling back to the controller. The ArgoCD namespace never gets an entry.

Three things are needed outside this chart:

  1. ArgoCD 3.5+, where impersonation is beta. Enable it with application.sync.impersonation.enabled: "true" in argocd-cm (on OpenShift GitOps, via ArgoCD.spec.extraConfig).

  2. The ServiceAccount in every tenant namespace, bound to that namespace's edit ClusterRole. An MTO Template + TemplateGroupInstance selecting the stakater.com/tenant label does it once for every tenant:

    apiVersion: tenantoperator.stakater.com/v1alpha1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: argocd-deployer
resources:
  manifests:
    - apiVersion: v1
      kind: ServiceAccount
      metadata: { name: argocd-deployer }
    - apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
      kind: RoleBinding
      metadata: { name: argocd-deployer-edit }
      roleRef: { apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io, kind: ClusterRole, name: edit }
      subjects:
        - { kind: ServiceAccount, name: argocd-deployer }

  3. A reduced controller ClusterRole, for real damage limitation. Otherwise impersonation enforces tenant boundaries at sync time while the controller still holds cluster-admin.

ArgoCD picks the account by the Application's destination namespace, and the template above grants it edit in that namespace only. So two kinds of Application stop syncing: one carrying a cluster-scoped kind from clusterResourceWhitelist (such as a Namespace), and one whose manifests write into another namespace. Grant those rights to argocd-deployer deliberately, or keep such Applications out of tenant projects.

Previous: Applications in tenant namespaces · Next: Security

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: For a platform administrator: install the chart once, then opt tenants in. The whole setup is cluster-wide — there is no per-tenant installation step.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Multi-Tenant Operator Tenant v1beta3 and IntegrationConfig v1beta1 Template Operator v2 (templates.v2.stakater.com) Required — the extension is configuration for it and does nothing without it. 0.0.8 recommended; 0.0.7+ keeps AppProjects on teardown (see Operating); strict drift protection (the default) needs its sync webhook ArgoCD argoproj.io/v1alpha1 AppProject; 3.x, tested on 3.5.4 Kubernetes 1.33+ tested. Template Operator v2's CRDs do not install on 1.31

docs.title: ArgoCD versions
docs.text:
Upstream ArgoCD supports the last three minors. OpenShift GitOps 1.22 ships ArgoCD 3.5, 1.21 ships 3.4, 1.20 ships 3.3. Some features need a specific line:

Feature Needs this chart, security defaults included ArgoCD 3.0+ Applications in the tenant's own namespace ArgoCD 3.x. 3-segment RBAC (<project>/<namespace>/<app>) needs 3.4.4+ a name on clusterResourceWhitelist entries ArgoCD 3.3+ sync impersonation (beta); ApplicationSets in any namespace (stable) ArgoCD 3.5+ / OpenShift GitOps 1.22

docs.title: Install Template Operator v2
docs.text:
The extension renders custom resources for Template Operator v2, so it must be running first — without it, nothing the chart installs is reconciled. The simplest route is to let MTO deploy it: set components.templateOperatorV2.mode: Managed in the IntegrationConfig.

spec:
  components:
    templateOperatorV2:
      mode: Managed

MTO then runs Template Operator v2 in multi-tenant-operator as the ServiceAccount tenant-operator-template-operator-v2 — the values used below. To install it yourself from its Helm chart instead, it runs as template-operator-v2 in stakater-template-operator; set rbac.serviceAccount to match.

docs.title: Install the extension
docs.text:
argocd.namespace is required (where AppProjects are created), and rbac.serviceAccount must match your Template Operator's identity.

helm install mto-extension-argocd \
  oci://ghcr.io/stakater/public/charts/mto-extension-argocd \
  --namespace multi-tenant-operator \
  --set argocd.namespace=openshift-gitops \
  --set rbac.serviceAccount.name=tenant-operator-template-operator-v2 \
  --set rbac.serviceAccount.namespace=multi-tenant-operator

The ServiceAccount must be your Template Operator's

The RBAC the chart installs binds to rbac.serviceAccount. If it names an account that is not the one Template Operator runs as, helm install still succeeds but nothing reconciles — the parent cannot even list Tenants. The values above are for an MTO-managed Template Operator; a standalone install uses template-operator-v2 in stakater-template-operator.

Nothing is created for a tenant yet — scaffolding.mode defaults to OnAnnotation, so a tenant is included only once it opts in.

docs.title: Opt a tenant in
docs.text:
The value must be exactly "true"; "True", "yes" and "1" all read as opted out, deliberately.

kubectl annotate tenant acme argocd.tenantoperator.stakater.com/enabled=true

scaffolding.mode also offers OnLabel (a label instead of an annotation), Always (every tenant), and Never (none). See Reference.

Roll out gradually

Keep the default OnAnnotation and opt in one tenant first. Confirm its AppProject looks right, then opt in the rest. Switching to Always later brings every tenant in at once; narrowing the mode again removes the projects it now excludes (see Operating → what deletes an AppProject), so change it deliberately.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
One row per opted-in tenant:

kubectl get templateinstances.templates.v2.stakater.com \
  -n multi-tenant-operator -l templates.v2.stakater.com/instance \
  -o custom-columns='TENANT:.spec.parameters[?(@.name=="tenant")].value,READY:.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status'

TENANT   READY
acme     True

Tip

Always use the fully-qualified templateinstances.templates.v2.stakater.com. On OpenShift, a bare kubectl get templateinstance resolves to OpenShift's own template.openshift.io kind and returns the wrong object with an empty status — which looks exactly like "nothing is reconciling".

Previous: Overview · Next: Giving a tenant an AppProject

docs.title: Migrating from the Extensions integration
docs.text: The older ArgoCD integration is configured through the Extensions custom resource and IntegrationConfig.spec.integrations.argocd, reconciled by MTO's built-in ExtensionsArgoCDReconciler (see the older page). This extension replaces both. It renders the same per-tenant AppProject, so a migration is a change of mechanism, not of outcome — and you can start from a compatibility shape that matches the old output, then move to the secure defaults.

docs.title: What changes
docs.text:
Old (Extensions + built-in reconciler) This extension Per-tenant config an Extensions CR per tenant an opt-in annotation/label on the Tenant Cluster-wide config IntegrationConfig.spec.integrations.argocd chart values Who reconciles MTO's Go controller Template Operator, from the chart Defaults the ArgoCD namespace is a destination; broad roles neither (least privilege)

integrations.argocd.{namespace, clusterResourceWhitelist, namespaceResourceBlacklist} are no longer read by this extension; move those values into the chart (argocd.namespace, argocd.clusterResourceWhitelist, argocd.namespaceResourceBlacklist). accessControl.privileged in the IntegrationConfig is still read.

docs.title: Start from the compatibility shape
docs.text:
Two values make the rendered AppProject match the old controller's output, so you can cut over without changing what any tenant can do:

argocd:
  allowControlPlaneDestination: true   # keep the ArgoCD namespace as a destination
roles:
  profile: extensionsCompatible        # the legacy broad role shape

Install with these, confirm each tenant's AppProject is equivalent, then remove the Extensions CRs and the integrations.argocd block.

docs.title: Then move to the secure defaults
docs.text:
Drop the two compatibility values and re-render. Each managed AppProject then changes:

  • the ArgoCD namespace leaves destinations — Applications that deploy into the control-plane namespace stop syncing. Move them into tenant namespaces first (see Applications in tenant namespaces), or migrate them deliberately.
  • the roles narrow to least privilege (edit can no longer create/delete/override Applications; exec is off).

Do this as a deliberate, announced step — it is a real tightening of what tenants can do.

docs.title: Deliberate differences from the old output
docs.text:
Even in compatibility mode, a few differences are intentional (each is pinned by the extension's equivalence tests):

  • spec.description is Managed by mto-extension-argocd.
  • roles[].groups gains the tenant's users alongside its groups (a name listed twice appears once; ArgoCD rejects a duplicate). This is a fix — the generated group only resolves where ArgoCD is told which claim carries it (see Security).
  • roles[].policies are one line per project-scoped resource instead of one line with resource *. Same access; ArgoCD's API rejects * there, so the old single-line form actually broke every project write through ArgoCD (including create-token and the UI).
  • metadata carries a templates.v2.stakater.com/deletion-policy: Orphan annotation when purge is off, and does not carry MTO's multi-tenant-operator/predicate label.

See Security for the defaults and Operating for what teardown does.

Previous: Reference

docs.title: Operating
docs.text: Day-2 for a platform administrator: how drift is handled, how to check every tenant at once, what removes a project, and how to upgrade and uninstall safely.

docs.title: Drift protection
docs.text:
sync.mode defaults to strict: a managed AppProject cannot be hand-edited or deleted — Template Operator's admission webhook refuses both. Under the looser revert, a hand-deleted AppProject wedges in Terminating forever while its TemplateInstance still reports healthy, so strict is the right default.

argocd proj role create-token and delete-token still work: ArgoCD writes tokens into spec.roles[].jwtTokens, which the chart exempts from enforcement. A later re-render drops that spec copy (roles are applied as one list), but the token stays valid — ArgoCD checks project tokens against status.jwtTokensByRole, which Template Operator does not touch.

docs.title: Fleet health
docs.text:
One object answers for every tenant. This prints nothing when all is well, and one line per unhealthy tenant with the real error:

kubectl get templateinstances.templates.v2.stakater.com mto-argocd-parent \
  -n multi-tenant-operator -o json \
  | jq -r '.status.outputs as $o | $o.ready | keys[] as $k
      | select(($o.ready[$k]|fromjson|join("")) != "True")
      | "\($k): \($o.errors[$k]|fromjson|join(" | "))"'

The errors field collects every failing condition's message, whichever stage broke — parameter resolution, rendering or apply — because the Ready condition only ever summarises ("Template rendering failed").

Tip

Use the fully-qualified templateinstances.templates.v2.stakater.com. On OpenShift a bare kubectl get templateinstance returns OpenShift's own kind with an empty status — indistinguishable from "not reconciling".

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
A tenant has no AppProject. Most common first, each independent of the others:

  • The tenant has not opted in (scaffolding.mode is OnAnnotation/OnLabel and the annotation/label is missing or not exactly "true").
  • rbac.serviceAccount does not match Template Operator v2's identity, so the parent cannot list Tenants — check mto-argocd-parent's Ready condition (Installation).
  • The tenant has a malformed override annotation: only that tenant's child fails; the fleet-health query above names it.

Nothing reconciles for any tenant (no AppProjects at all). The parent cannot read its inputs — almost always the wrong rbac.serviceAccount (above), a missing IntegrationConfig, or a Kubernetes/Template Operator version mismatch (Installation). Read mto-argocd-parent's conditions.

An edit to an AppProject is rejected with a sync-enforcement webhook error. That is sync.mode: strict working as intended — the Tenant is the only place to change what the extension produces. See Drift protection.

docs.title: What deletes an AppProject
docs.text:
Template Operator owns every object a child renders. When the parent stops rendering a tenant's child — the tenant opts out, scaffolding.mode narrows, the Tenant is deleted, or helm uninstall runs — the child and its AppProject are removed, unless the AppProject is marked to be kept.

With onDeletePurgeAppProject: false (the default) the chart marks each AppProject templates.v2.stakater.com/deletion-policy: Orphan. Template Operator 0.0.7+ honours the mark and releases the project (the object stays, without the finalizer/labels, and ArgoCD keeps using it).

Trigger 0.0.7+, purge off (default) purge on 0.0.6 and earlier opt-in removed / Tenant deleted / scaffolding.mode narrowed / helm uninstall released deleted deleted

Warning

On Template Operator 0.0.6 and earlier, onDeletePurgeAppProject: false has no effect — the AppProject is deleted in every case above. Use 0.0.7+ to keep projects.

"Purge on" is onDeletePurgeAppProject: true, or the on-delete-purge annotation on one Tenant.

These do not delete an AppProject: a malformed override annotation (only that child fails), a tenant losing all its namespaces (it keeps the project), or the parent failing to render (Template Operator keeps the last rendered set, so a broken IntegrationConfig cannot wipe the fleet).

docs.title: Upgrading the chart
docs.text:
helm upgrade re-renders every tenant's AppProject in place — the object's UID does not change, so ArgoCD keeps using it. A values change (new repos, a tightened profile) therefore reaches every tenant on the next render.

Two upgrades change the rendered projects on purpose, so make them deliberately and announce them:

  • Moving off the compatibility shape (dropping argocd.allowControlPlaneDestination / roles.profile: extensionsCompatible) removes the control-plane destination and narrows the roles. See Migrating.
  • Narrowing scaffolding.mode removes the projects for every tenant the new mode excludes — see what deletes an AppProject.

Check the chart's release notes before a major version bump; a renamed child TemplateInstance is called out there, because it releases and re-creates each project.

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text:
A plain helm uninstall is safe:

helm uninstall mto-extension-argocd -n multi-tenant-operator

The chart's RBAC is kept on uninstall (helm.sh/resource-policy: keep, and Prune=false,Delete=false for an ArgoCD-managed release), so Template Operator keeps the permissions its finalizers need while it reaps the children. What then happens to the AppProjects depends on the version and purge, as above. The NOTES.txt that helm install prints has the commands to remove the kept RBAC afterwards.

Reinstalling immediately fails with an ownership-metadata error — wait for Template/mto-argocd-parent to disappear first.

Previous: Security · Next: Reference

docs.title: ArgoCD
docs.text:
Give every tenant its own ArgoCD AppProject — scoped to the tenant's namespaces, with owner, edit and view roles — derived from the Tenant you already maintain and kept in sync as it changes.

Note

This is the Helm-chart ArgoCD extension (mto-extension-argocd). It replaces the built-in ArgoCD integration configured through the Extensions resource, now deprecated — see the older integration and Migrating.

Requires Template Operator v2

The extension is configuration for Template Operator v2 (custom resources in the templates.v2.stakater.com API group) — it installs no controller of its own and does nothing until Template Operator v2 reconciles it. Template Operator v2 must be running on the cluster; MTO can deploy it for you. See Installation.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
You maintain The extension keeps in sync a Tenant one AppProject per tenant and opt it in (one annotation) scoped to the tenant's namespaces owner / edit / view roles, bound to its groups and users the repositories it may deploy from the cluster-scoped kinds it may manage

You write — a Tenant, opted in:

apiVersion: tenantoperator.stakater.com/v1beta3
kind: Tenant
metadata:
  name: acme
  annotations:
    argocd.tenantoperator.stakater.com/enabled: "true"   # opt in
spec:
  accessControl:
    owners:
      groups: [acme-admins]
      users:  [alice@acme.example]
  namespaces:
    withTenantPrefix: [dev, prod]

You get — one AppProject, kept in sync (abridged):

apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: AppProject
metadata:
  name: acme
  namespace: openshift-gitops
spec:
  destinations:                       # the tenant's namespaces — never the control plane
    - { namespace: acme-dev,  server: https://kubernetes.default.svc }
    - { namespace: acme-prod, server: https://kubernetes.default.svc }
  roles:                              # bound to the tenant's groups and users
    - { name: acme-owner, ... }       # full access to acme/*
    - { name: acme-edit,  ... }       # get, sync, update
    - { name: acme-view,  ... }       # get
  sourceRepos: [ https://github.com/acme/acme-gitops ]

No AppProject YAML and no hand-written ArgoCD RBAC — and nothing is created for a tenant until it opts in.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The chart installs no operator of its own. It renders three Template Operator v2 objects — a parent Template, a child Template, and one parent TemplateInstance — and Template Operator v2 reconciles one AppProject per tenant.

flowchart LR
    T[Tenants] --> P
    N[Namespaces] --> P
    IC[IntegrationConfig] --> P
    P["parent<br/>TemplateInstance"] -- one child per opted-in tenant --> C["child<br/>TemplateInstance"]
    C -- renders --> A["one AppProject<br/>per tenant"]
    A --> ARGO[ArgoCD]

The parent reads every Tenant, every Namespace, and the IntegrationConfig — three cluster-wide watches regardless of tenant count — and emits one child per opted-in tenant. A namespace event affecting one tenant rewrites only that tenant's project.

docs.title: Who does what
docs.text:
Platform administrator Tenant Sets up installs the chart; sets argocd.namespace, repos, resource limits — Per tenant nothing — opt-in is one annotation opts in; creates Applications in its project Never hand-writes an AppProject or ArgoCD RBAC touches ArgoCD RBAC, or reaches another tenant's project

The division is the point: a tenant gets self-service GitOps scoped to itself, and the platform team maintains no per-tenant ArgoCD configuration.

docs.title: How roles map to ArgoCD access
docs.text:
Each Tenant access level becomes one AppProject role, at least privilege by default (roles.profile: leastPrivilege):

Tenant level ArgoCD role applications applicationsets repositories / clusters / logs owners <tenant>-owner full (*) full (*) get (repos *) editors <tenant>-edit get, sync, update, action/* get get viewers <tenant>-view get get get

Edit cannot create, delete or override Applications, and the web terminal (exec) is off unless you enable it for owners. The legacy, broader shape exists for migration only — see Security and Migrating.

Built on Template Operator

Because the extension renders through Template Operator, the permissions the chart grants are shared with anyone who can author a Template. On a cluster where tenants (or others) can create Templates, read Security → how the extension scopes Template Operator v2 before going to production.

docs.text:

  8. Migrating — from the deprecated Extensions integration

Next: Installation

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: The full, commented reference is the chart's values.yaml. This page covers the values and overrides you reach for most.

docs.title: Chart values
docs.text: Value Default argocd.namespace — Required. Where AppProjects are created rbac.serviceAccount.name / .namespace template-operator-v2 / stakater-template-operator Template Operator's identity. Set to match your install — see Installation scaffolding.mode OnAnnotation Always, OnLabel, OnAnnotation, Never argocd.sourceRepos.pattern [] Per-tenant repo patterns, one sourceRepos entry each; {{ tenant }} is expanded argocd.clusterResourceWhitelist [] Cluster-scoped kinds tenants may manage — read Cluster-scoped kinds first argocd.namespaceResourceBlacklist [] Namespaced kinds they may not sync.mode strict Drift protection — see Operating onDeletePurgeAppProject false Keep (false) or delete (true) the AppProject on teardown argocd.allowControlPlaneDestination false The legacy, unsafe shape — see Security argocd.allowClusterResourceNames false Allow a name on clusterResourceWhitelist entries. Set only on ArgoCD 3.3+ roles.profile leastPrivilege Or extensionsCompatible, the legacy shape roles.exec.enabled / roles.clusters.enabled false Owner-only web terminal, cluster writes argocd.sourceNamespaces.enabled / .pattern false / {{ tenant }}-argocd Applications in tenant namespaces argocd.impersonation.enabled / .serviceAccount false / argocd-deployer Sync impersonation identity.mode / identity.groupPattern accessControl / tenant-{{ tenant }}-{{ tier }} Groups named by pattern argocd.syncWindows [] Sync windows on every project argocd.orphanedResources off warn or monitor to flag resources no Application manages

docs.title: Per-tenant overrides
docs.text:
Six settings can be overridden per tenant, as annotations under argocd.tenantoperator.stakater.com/:

Annotation Overrides Format source-repos argocd.sourceRepos.pattern JSON array of strings cluster-resource-whitelist argocd.clusterResourceWhitelist JSON array of {group, kind, name?} namespace-resource-blacklist argocd.namespaceResourceBlacklist JSON array of {group, kind} on-delete-purge onDeletePurgeAppProject "true" or "false" sync-windows argocd.syncWindows JSON array of window objects orphaned-resources argocd.orphanedResources off, warn or monitor

An absent annotation inherits the chart default. An explicit [] overrides with empty — a different thing — which is why the value is passed to the child verbatim rather than parsed by the parent; malformed JSON fails that tenant's child alone and never falls back to the default. Override values are shape-checked, not value-checked — see Security.

docs.title: Cluster-scoped kinds
docs.text: A cluster-scoped kind on the allow-list is granted for every object of that kind in the cluster. Prefer exact names (ArgoCD 3.3+, with argocd.allowClusterResourceNames: true) over globs, and read Security → Cluster-scoped kinds are cluster-wide before allowing any.

docs.title: The opt-in annotation value
docs.text: scaffolding.mode: OnAnnotation/OnLabel includes a tenant only when argocd.tenantoperator.stakater.com/enabled is exactly "true". "True", "yes", "1" and "on" all read as opted out, deliberately.

docs.title: One release per cluster
docs.text:
Install the chart once per cluster. Its Template and RBAC object names are fixed (mto-argocd-parent, mto-argocd-child, and the mto-extension-argocd-* roles), so a second release fails with an invalid ownership metadata error. A single release already serves every tenant, and the parent reads the one cluster-wide IntegrationConfig, so two releases — even in different namespaces — would collide on it. To target more than one ArgoCD instance from one cluster, raise it with the maintainers; it is not supported by a second install.

Previous: Operating · Next: Migrating

docs.title: Security
docs.text: The extension's defaults are least privilege. This page explains the ones that matter and the things that can look correct while being unsafe.

docs.title: The ArgoCD namespace is never a tenant destination
docs.text:
An Application in the control-plane namespace may reference any AppProject, and the application controller that syncs it is cluster-admin — so a tenant able to deploy there could create Applications, AppProjects or repository/cluster Secrets for every project, which is ArgoCD admin. The AppProject does not need the ArgoCD namespace as a destination: it lives there whatever destinations says.

argocd.allowControlPlaneDestination: true restores the legacy shape (the ArgoCD namespace as a destination). It is unsafe and exists for migration only.

docs.title: Roles are least privilege
docs.text:
With roles.profile: leastPrivilege (the default):

Role applications applicationsets exec owner * * off (create with roles.exec.enabled) edit get, sync, update, update/*, action/* get off view get get off

Edit cannot create, delete or override Applications. ArgoCD's web terminal runs as the argocd-server ServiceAccount — outside the tenant's own RBAC and audit trail — so exec is off unless you enable it (owner only). roles.profile: extensionsCompatible restores the legacy broad */get shape, for migration only; consider also setting application.sync.requireOverridePrivilegeForRevisionSync in ArgoCD (3.2+).

docs.title: Cluster-scoped kinds are cluster-wide
docs.text:
A cluster-scoped kind on the allow-list is granted for every object of that kind in the cluster, and the controller that syncs it is cluster-admin. With {group: "", kind: Namespace}, a tenant can change or delete any namespace — another tenant's, or kube-system — and can move a namespace into its own destinations by setting its stakater.com/tenant label.

Since ArgoCD 3.3 an entry can take a name (a glob). Older ArgoCD drops the field on apply, turning the entry back into "every object of this kind", so the chart refuses a name unless argocd.allowClusterResourceNames: true confirms 3.3+. Use exact names; a prefix glob is not tenant-safe ({{ tenant }}-* for acme also matches acme-corp-prod). See Reference.

docs.title: Per-tenant overrides are as trusted as the Tenant
docs.text: A Tenant can override its repositories and resource lists by annotation (Reference). Those values are shape-checked but not value-checked, so whoever can annotate a Tenant can widen that tenant's access up to what the annotations allow. Keep Tenant write access with the platform, and treat anyone who can annotate a Tenant as trusted with its ArgoCD access.

docs.title: How the extension scopes Template Operator v2
docs.text:
The extension renders through Template Operator v2, which applies objects with its own ServiceAccount. This chart grants that account least privilege — it may write AppProjects only in the ArgoCD namespace (through a RoleBinding scoped there) and otherwise only read — so there is no broad, cluster-wide write for a stray Template to misuse, and nothing extra for you to install.

Keep one administrative rule: authoring a Template Operator v2 Template is a privileged operation — anyone who can create Templates and TemplateInstances drives the operator. MTO's tenant roles do not grant that, and it should not be granted to tenants.

docs.title: Before production
docs.text:
Four ways to end up with something that looks correct and isn't:

  • Seed the resource lists. clusterResourceWhitelist and namespaceResourceBlacklist are chart values; if you forget them every tenant's project silently loses both lists.
  • Set sourceRepos. A project with none permits no repository — see Giving a tenant an AppProject.
  • List real groups and users. roles[].groups gets the MTO-generated group first, but MTO only creates it when the tenant-operator runs with PLATFORM_TYPE=Openshift. A tenant whose owners are only that group gets a project granting access to nobody.

docs.title: Match users the way your login provides them
docs.text:
The chart adds the tenant's users to roles[].groups, e.g. alice@acme.example. ArgoCD compares that with the login token's user ID and the claims named in argocd-rbac-cm scopes (default [groups]). Behind Dex the user ID is an opaque value, not an email, so with the default the user entries grant nothing. Add the claim that carries the user name the Tenant uses — usually email:

# argocd-rbac-cm, in the ArgoCD namespace
data:
  scopes: '[groups, email]'

ArgoCD reloads it without a restart. Only include a claim users cannot change themselves in the identity provider, and note the setting is global (email entries in policy.csv start to match too, and a user in a project role can create tokens for that role).

Previous: Identity and sync impersonation · Next: Operating

docs.title: Design rules
docs.text:
The tutorial extension works. This page is about making one that is safe to run against every tenant on a production cluster.

Every rule here comes from building Stakater's ArgoCD and Vault Enterprise extensions. Most started as a bug that hit every tenant at once, or failed silently.

docs.title: Know your blast radius
docs.text:
An extension has two failure domains, and each rule below keeps a failure in the smaller one.

A failure in Affects So A child One tenant It is visible on that tenant's TemplateInstance, and every other tenant carries on. The parent Every tenant at once Make it as hard to break as you can. A chart value Every tenant at once, after install Refuse a bad value at helm install, not later on the cluster.

There is a worse case than a failed render: a render that succeeds with the wrong output. template-operator-v2 deletes whatever a render no longer contains. If a typo makes the parent emit no children, every child is deleted, and with them every object they rendered, for every tenant. Most of the rules below come back to this.

docs.title: The operator's ServiceAccount is the boundary
docs.text:
Everything your chart grants goes to Template Operator v2's ServiceAccount, and the operator applies every Template's rendered objects with that one ServiceAccount — into whatever namespace the manifest names, not limited by targetNamespaces. This is by design: the RBAC of that ServiceAccount is the security boundary.

For an extension author that means two rules:

  • Grant least privilege, scoped to the namespaces you actually write to. Confine the mutating verbs to the operator namespace and the specific namespaces your children render into; keep only list/watch cluster-wide (for teardown). Do not grant the operator broad, cluster-wide write — that is what makes the shared ServiceAccount a cross-tenant path.
  • Treat Template authorship as a privileged operation. Anyone who can create a Template + TemplateInstance drives the operator with those permissions. MTO's tenant roles do not grant that; do not grant Template Operator v2's template-editor/templateinstance-editor roles to tenants.

Scoping the grant is the fix. Where a broadly-permissioned operator is unavoidable, the platform can add a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy that confines the operator's writes to the owning TemplateInstance's namespace as defence-in-depth — it is documented, with the policy, under Template Operator v2 → Security. It is optional, not a substitute for scoping the RBAC.

docs.title: Write the parent so it cannot fail
docs.text:
Every tenant flows through the parent's single render.

Read optional keys with index. From template-operator-v2 0.0.8, a field read of a missing key fails the render. $t.metadata.annotations on a Tenant without annotations takes the whole parent down. index returns nothing for a missing key; default dict turns that into an empty map:

{{- $annotations := default dict (index $t.metadata "annotations") }}

Default each level in turn. dig looks like a shortcut, but it fails on an explicit null, and Tenants do arrive with spec: null or accessControl: null. The ArgoCD extension tested every shape. Only this form survives all of them:

{{- $spec := default dict (index $t "spec") }}
{{- $ac := default dict (index $spec "accessControl") }}
{{- $owners := default dict (index $ac "owners") }}
{{- $groups := default list (index $owners "groups") }}

Pass per-tenant input down as raw text. If a tenant's annotation holds JSON, the parent copies the string into the child's parameter and the child decodes it. Malformed JSON then fails one child instead of the parent.

Decide present-or-absent with hasKey, not default. default treats "" as unset. An author who writes an empty annotation clearly meant to override something, so that should fail loudly, not quietly fall back to the chart default:

{{- $value := $chartDefault }}
{{- if hasKey $annotations $key }}{{- $value = index $annotations $key }}{{- end }}

Make one pass over large lists. A loop over namespaces inside a loop over tenants costs tenants × namespaces steps, and the parent re-renders on every Namespace event in the cluster. At 300 tenants and 3,000 namespaces, the ArgoCD extension measured 1.9 seconds per render with nested loops. Bucket namespaces by tenant in one pass instead.

Never let a tenant's name collide with yours. Name children under a prefix the parent's own name cannot take. If children were named <extension>-<tenant>, a Tenant called parent would produce <extension>-parent, the parent TemplateInstance itself. template-operator-v2 would overwrite the parent with that child, the parent would stop ranging over tenants, and every other child would be deleted. Use <extension>-tenant-<tenant>.

docs.title: Validate in the child
docs.text:
The child is where a tenant's input gets checked, because a failure there stays with that tenant.

  • Decode with mustFromJson. Plain fromJson hides the error and returns an error map, which renders into a live object.
  • Check the shape, not only the syntax. [{"group":{}}] is valid JSON. Rendered with quote, it becomes the string "map[]" and applies cleanly to the live object. Check each value's kind (kindIs "string", kindIs "slice", kindIs "map") and fail if it is wrong.
  • Accept exactly the values you mean. For a boolean, accept "true" and "false" and fail on anything else. True, yes, 1 and on all look affirmative. Treating them as "no" silently does the opposite of what the author meant.
  • Say what is wrong. The fail message appears in the tenant's TemplateInstance status. Name the annotation and the bad value.

docs.title: Fail closed
docs.text:
When an input decides who can reach what, a missing value must stop the render, not fall back to something permissive.

The ArgoCD extension reads the IntegrationConfig's privileged namespaces and keeps them out of every tenant's AppProject. An early version read them with a default, along these lines:

{{- $privNs := dig "accessControl" "privileged" "namespaces" list $ic }}

When the field is absent, that yields an empty list. An empty list filters nothing, so privileged namespaces went into every tenant's destinations. The version that ships refuses instead:

{{- $priv := default dict (index (default dict (index $ic "accessControl")) "privileged") }}
{{- if or (not (hasKey $priv "namespaces")) (kindIs "invalid" (index $priv "namespaces")) }}
{{- fail "IntegrationConfig .spec.accessControl.privileged.namespaces is absent or null; refusing to render. Set it explicitly, to [] if the cluster has none." }}
{{- end }}

The same reasoning gives three more rules:

  • No defaultValue on a security-relevant valueFrom. A default masks a failed read, and the failure mode is cross-tenant access.
  • Reject an empty regular expression. "" is a valid pattern that matches everything, so one stray entry in a deny list removes every tenant's access, or, in an allow list, grants everything.
  • Use mustRegexMatch on patterns that come from configuration. The plain form turns an invalid pattern into "no match", which disables the filter for every tenant.

docs.title: Validate chart values twice
docs.text:
A chart value applies to every tenant, so check it at helm install, before anything renders. Check it twice:

  1. In values.schema.json, for the user's benefit.
  2. In a template guard that calls fail. The schema can be skipped (helm install --skip-schema-validation), and some tools that render charts through the Helm SDK never apply it.

Values that most need a guard:

  • True-or-false values. In a Go template, the string "false" is true. A toggle set to "false" turns the feature on. Check with kindIs "bool".
  • Enumerations. The ArgoCD extension's scaffolding.mode decides which tenants get a child. A typo matches no branch, every tenant fails the filter, no children are emitted, and every AppProject is deleted. Check it against the list of valid values.
  • Keys you look up. An empty annotation key never matches anything, so the opt-in or the override it names is silently ignored.
  • Placeholders. If a value supports {{ tenant }}, reject any other placeholder syntax ({{ .tenant }}, ${tenant}, %s). Otherwise it ships verbatim into every tenant's objects.
  • sync.mode: strict without metadata.finalizers in ignoreFields. Teardown then deadlocks.
{{- define "my-extension.validate" -}}
{{- if not (has .Values.scaffolding.mode (list "Always" "OnLabel" "OnAnnotation" "Never")) -}}
{{- fail (printf "scaffolding.mode must be one of Always, OnLabel, OnAnnotation, Never; got %q. Any other value emits no children, and every tenant's objects are deleted." .Values.scaffolding.mode) -}}
{{- end -}}
{{- end -}}

docs.title: Opting tenants in
docs.text:
Choose how a tenant gets the extension. The ArgoCD extension offers four modes, and the same set works for most extensions:

Mode A tenant gets the extension when OnAnnotation (default) it has the opt-in annotation set to exactly "true" OnLabel it has the opt-in label set to exactly "true" Always it exists Never never. Existing objects are removed, as below.

Default to opt-in. On a cluster that already has these objects managed some other way, an opt-in extension changes nothing until someone asks it to.

Narrowing the filter removes objects. If a tenant stops matching, its child is no longer emitted, so template-operator-v2 deletes it and everything it rendered. Document that next to the setting, and see Deletion.

docs.title: Decide who controls each input
docs.text:
An extension turns cluster state into access in another system. For each input, write down who can change it.

  • The Tenant resource is normally edited only by platform administrators. Overrides read from Tenant annotations are as trusted as the Tenant.
  • The stakater.com/tenant label on a namespace says which tenant owns it. If the extension grants access to whatever is labelled for a tenant, then anyone who can set that label can claim the tenant's access. Keep namespace labelling under the platform's control. Tenant users must not hold patch or update on Namespaces at cluster scope. MTO needs the same rule for its own isolation.
  • Objects inside tenant namespaces, such as ServiceAccount annotations, can be written by the tenant's own users. An extension that reads them, as Vault Enterprise does, must treat them as untrusted input and cap what they can request.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
Names you compose from tenant data must be unambiguous.

  • Join name parts with a character the parts cannot contain. With hyphens, namespace t-web plus ServiceAccount api-x and namespace t-web-api plus ServiceAccount x both give t-web-api-x. The Vault Enterprise extension joins with dots (kv.<tenant>.<namespace>.<serviceaccount>), because none of the parts may contain one.
  • Give each family of names its own prefix and part count, so that a name from one family can never equal a name from another.
  • Quote every value derived from a tenant name. 1234 is a valid tenant name and a YAML number.
  • Check tenant names that become identifiers elsewhere. The Tenant CRD does not restrict names to what your tool accepts. Vault Enterprise skips a tenant whose name is not a DNS label, and lists each skipped tenant and the reason in a ConfigMap, instead of failing the parent.

docs.title: Deletion
docs.text:
template-operator-v2 deletes an object as soon as no render contains it. That happens when a tenant opts out, when a filter narrows, when the parent's TemplateInstance is deleted, and when a bug produces an empty render. Decide, per kind, whether that is acceptable.

If deleting the object Then loses nothing; it is recreated identically Let template-operator-v2 delete it. breaks people who depend on it, but loses no data Annotate it templates.v2.stakater.com/deletion-policy: Orphan, so it is released instead of deleted. Consider making that a per-tenant choice. destroys data, such as a Vault namespace and its secrets Do not rely on Kubernetes alone. Also protect it in the tool itself.

The ArgoCD extension orphans AppProjects by default, because deleting one strands every Application that uses it. Purging is an opt-in value that a tenant can override.

The Vault Enterprise extension goes further. A tenant's Vault namespace and its secrets are rendered by the parent, for every valid Tenant, so they live as long as the Tenant resource rather than as long as its namespaces. On top of that, the production Vault policy that vault-config-operator logs in with denies delete on namespaces and mounts. A deleted CR then stays in Terminating and the data stays in Vault until an administrator decides.

docs.title: Uninstall in the right order
docs.text:
kubectl -n <namespace> delete templateinstances.templates.v2.stakater.com <parent> --wait
kubectl -n <namespace> wait templateinstances.templates.v2.stakater.com \
  -l templates.v2.stakater.com/instance=<parent> --for=delete --timeout=5m
helm uninstall <release> -n <namespace>
kubectl delete <the RBAC kept by the chart>

Deleting the parent TemplateInstance deletes its children, and they delete their objects. That takes time, and it needs the RBAC. So:

  • Mark the RBAC helm.sh/resource-policy: keep. If ArgoCD manages the chart, also mark it argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false,Delete=false. Otherwise helm uninstall, or an ArgoCD prune, removes the RBAC in the same step as the parent. template-operator-v2 is then forbidden from removing its finalizers, and everything stays in Terminating.
  • Keep reap permissions separate from create. If a "disable" value removes all the RBAC, template-operator-v2 can no longer delete what it already owns. Gate create on the value; keep get, update, patch and delete unconditional.
  • Keep anything a downstream controller needs to clean up. The Vault Enterprise chart creates the ServiceAccount that vault-config-operator logs in with. If that ServiceAccount goes before the CRs, vault-config-operator fails every delete and every CR stays in Terminating.

docs.title: Report health honestly
docs.text:
A child that is Ready means its objects were applied. It does not mean your tool accepted them.

  • Read the tool's own status back through outputs, so the TemplateInstance shows what happened downstream.
  • Know what that status can say. The status vault-config-operator writes cannot tell you whether an object is healthy now. It sets ReconcileSuccessful and ReconcileFailed side by side, and their timestamps stop moving after the first write. Vault Enterprise's outputs therefore say "has succeeded at least once" and "last error ever", and its docs say exactly that.
  • Aggregate in the parent. A fromAll output over the child TemplateInstances gives one object that answers whether every tenant is reconciled, and why not.

docs.title: Test it
docs.text:
Test at four levels. Each catches failures the level above it cannot.

Level Needs Catches helm lint and the chart-value guards nothing Chart structure, and bad values refused at install Render tests Go, no cluster Wrong output for a given set of Tenants, and parent failures Admission tests envtest and template-operator-v2's CRDs Templates the API server would reject: schema and CEL rules End-to-end a kind cluster with template-operator-v2 What template-operator-v2 and your tool actually do

docs.title: Render tests
docs.text:
Render tests are where most bugs are caught, and they are fast. Run your gotemplate files through the same function set template-operator-v2 uses, not through Helm. Helm adds functions such as toYaml, include and .Files, and replaces toJson and fromJson with its own versions. A gotemplate can pass under Helm and fail on the cluster.

template-operator-v2 0.0.8 renders with Sprig's text functions minus env, expandenv and getHostByName, and with missingkey=error. This engine reproduces that:

package render

import (
    "bytes"
    "errors"
    "io"
    "os"
    "text/template"

    "github.com/Masterminds/sprig/v3"
    "gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

func funcs() template.FuncMap {
    f := sprig.TxtFuncMap()
    delete(f, "env")
    delete(f, "expandenv")
    delete(f, "getHostByName")
    return f
}

// Render executes one gotemplate file against a parameter set.
func Render(path string, params map[string]any) ([]map[string]any, error) {
    src, err := os.ReadFile(path)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    t, err := template.New("template").Funcs(funcs()).Option("missingkey=error").Parse(string(src))
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    var out bytes.Buffer
    if err := t.Execute(&out, map[string]any{"parameters": params}); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    var docs []map[string]any
    dec := yaml.NewDecoder(&out)
    for {
        var d map[string]any
        if err := dec.Decode(&d); errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
            return docs, nil
        } else if err != nil {
            return nil, err
        }
        if len(d) > 0 {
            docs = append(docs, d)
        }
    }
}

Then table-drive the parent with the shapes Tenants really take. This is the tutorial's parent under test:

func TestParent(t *testing.T) {
    optIn := map[string]any{"tenant-info.example.com/enabled": "true"}
    cases := []struct {
        name       string
        tenants    []any
        namespaces []any
        children   []string
    }{
        {"no tenants", nil, nil, nil},
        {"not opted in", []any{tenant("acme", nil)}, []any{namespace("acme-dev", "acme")}, nil},
        {"near-miss opt-in", []any{tenant("acme", map[string]any{"tenant-info.example.com/enabled": "True"})}, nil, nil},
        {"opted in", []any{tenant("acme", optIn), tenant("globex", nil)},
            []any{namespace("acme-dev", "acme"), namespace("globex-dev", "globex")},
            []string{"tenant-info-tenant-acme"}},
        {"no namespaces", []any{tenant("initech", optIn)}, nil, []string{"tenant-info-tenant-initech"}},
        {"tenant named parent", []any{tenant("parent", optIn)}, nil, []string{"tenant-info-tenant-parent"}},
    }
    for _, tc := range cases {
        t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
            docs, err := Render("../../files/parent.tpl", parentParams(tc.tenants, tc.namespaces))
            if err != nil {
                t.Fatalf("parent failed, which fails every tenant: %v", err)
            }
            var got []string
            for _, d := range docs {
                got = append(got, d["metadata"].(map[string]any)["name"].(string))
            }
            if strings.Join(got, ",") != strings.Join(tc.children, ",") {
                t.Fatalf("children = %v, want %v", got, tc.children)
            }
        })
    }
}

tenant, namespace and parentParams are small helpers that build the maps a LIST returns. parentParams adds the parent's other parameters with the chart's default values. Feed each rendered child's parameters into the child gotemplate in the same way, and assert on the objects it renders and on the errors it should raise.

A test that cannot fail proves nothing. Break each guard on purpose and check that its test goes red. For example, change one index $t.metadata "annotations" in the parent to $t.metadata.annotations, and the "not opted in" case fails with map has no entry for key "annotations", the same error the cluster gives.

The ArgoCD extension adds three more kinds of render test:

  • Golden files: one fixture per scenario (a cluster's Tenants, Namespaces and IntegrationConfig, plus chart values), rendered and compared with a checked-in result.
  • Property tests: invariants over randomly generated clusters, such as "no tenant's destinations ever include another tenant's namespace".
  • A scale test: 1,000 tenants over about 8,000 namespaces must render within 10 seconds, which catches an accidentally quadratic loop.

docs.title: Admission and end-to-end tests
docs.text:
Admission tests start a real API server with envtest, install template-operator-v2's CRDs, and apply the Templates your chart renders. They catch what helm lint cannot: a field the CRD schema rejects, or a CEL rule on outputs or parameters. Vendor the CRDs at the template-operator-v2 version you support, and refresh them when you upgrade.

End-to-end tests run the tutorial's lab in CI, with your tool installed, and assert on what the tool does, not only on what was rendered. A useful order:

  1. Install the chart, then create tenants and namespaces.
  2. Assert on the tool's view. For example, log in to Vault as the workload's ServiceAccount and read its secret, or check that ArgoCD accepts the AppProject.
  3. Assert that one tenant cannot reach another tenant's objects. Pair every denial with a matching allowed request, so that a wrongly configured test cannot pass by being refused for the wrong reason.
  4. Opt a tenant out, and check that what should go goes and what should stay stays.
  5. Uninstall in the documented order, every run.

docs.title: Before you ship
docs.text:
• [ ] The parent survives Tenants with no annotations, no labels, spec: null and accessControl: null.
  • [ ] No per-tenant input is parsed in the parent.
  • [ ] Every security-relevant input fails closed when it is absent, null or empty.
  • [ ] Every chart value that affects all tenants is checked by a template guard, not only by the schema.
  • [ ] Child names cannot collide with the parent's.
  • [ ] RBAC grants list and watch at cluster scope on every rendered kind, and survives helm uninstall.
  • [ ] Your docs list every permission the chart grants template-operator-v2, and the cluster has the write-scope policy, with your namespace on its list.
  • [ ] sync: strict, with metadata.finalizers and any field your tool writes in ignoreFields.
  • [ ] Every kind has a deletion decision: delete, orphan, or protected in the tool.
  • [ ] Health is read back from the tool's own status, and documented for what it can and cannot say.
  • [ ] The uninstall order is documented and tested.
  • [ ] The template-operator-v2 version you tested against is pinned and written down.

docs.title: Build your own extension
docs.text:
The extensions in this section, such as ArgoCD and Vault, carry a tenant into a tool around the cluster. If your tool is not on the list, you can build the extension yourself, the same way Stakater builds its own.

An MTO extension is a Helm chart. It does not include an operator, a container image or a controller. The chart installs a few objects for template-operator-v2, and template-operator-v2 does the rest. It reads your Tenant resources, renders the objects your tool needs for each tenant, and keeps them in step as tenants change.

Stakater's ArgoCD and Vault Enterprise extensions are built this way, and this section is drawn from them.

docs.title: Is an extension the right tool?
docs.text:
An extension renders Kubernetes objects. It fits when the tool you are integrating is configured through Kubernetes resources:

The tool is configured by Example Extension? Its own CRDs, read by its own controller ArgoCD AppProject, Grafana operator GrafanaFolder, Kyverno Policy Yes. Render the CRs directly. An API, with an operator that maps CRs onto it Vault through vault-config-operator, Keycloak through its config operator Yes. Render that operator's CRs. Plain Kubernetes objects ConfigMap, NetworkPolicy, RoleBinding in each tenant namespace Yes, but first check whether MTO itself or a plain Template already does it. Only an HTTP API, with no operator in front of it A SaaS product's REST API Not on its own. template-operator-v2 only talks to the Kubernetes API, so something has to turn objects into API calls.

The Extensions concept page describes the other ways MTO reaches outside the cluster.

docs.title: How an extension works
docs.text:
An extension is built from two Templates. The parent reads the cluster and emits one child TemplateInstance for each tenant. The child renders that tenant's objects.

flowchart LR
    subgraph inputs[Read from the cluster]
        T[Tenant CRs]
        N[Namespaces]
        IC[IntegrationConfig]
    end
    subgraph chart[Installed by your Helm chart]
        PT[Template<br/>parent]
        CT[Template<br/>child]
        PTI[TemplateInstance<br/>parent]
        R[RBAC for<br/>template-operator-v2]
    end
    inputs -- watched --> PTI
    PTI -. uses .-> PT
    PTI -- renders one per tenant --> CTI[TemplateInstance<br/>child, per tenant]
    CTI -. uses .-> CT
    CTI -- renders --> O[Your tool's objects<br/>AppProject, Policy, ...]
Object Installed by Role Parent Template your chart A Go template that ranges over every Tenant and emits one child TemplateInstance per tenant that should get the extension. Parent TemplateInstance your chart The only instance you install. Its parameters read Tenants, Namespaces and anything else the parent needs, and template-operator-v2 watches them. Child Template your chart Renders one tenant's objects from parameters the parent sets. Child TemplateInstance the parent One per tenant. You never write these. RBAC your chart What template-operator-v2 may read and write for this extension. By default it can only manage Templates and TemplateInstances and read Namespaces.

What happens when a tenant changes:

sequenceDiagram
    actor Admin as Platform admin
    participant K as Kubernetes API
    participant TO as template-operator-v2
    participant Tool as Your tool's controller
    Admin->>K: annotate Tenant acme (opt in)
    K-->>TO: watch event on Tenant
    TO->>TO: re-render parent with every Tenant and Namespace
    TO->>K: apply child TemplateInstance for acme
    K-->>TO: new child TemplateInstance
    TO->>TO: render child with acme's parameters
    TO->>K: apply acme's objects (for example an AppProject)
    K-->>Tool: your tool's controller sees the object
    TO->>K: write status, conditions and outputs

Why two levels instead of one Template that renders everything:

  • One tenant's failure stays with that tenant. If a tenant has a malformed annotation, only its child fails. Every other tenant keeps reconciling.
  • The watch count does not grow with tenants. The parent holds a few cluster-wide watches, such as all Tenants and all Namespaces, however many tenants there are.
  • Status per tenant. Each child TemplateInstance reports its own conditions, so you can see which tenant is broken and why.
  • Changes stay small. A namespace event that affects one tenant rewrites only that tenant's child.

docs.title: Two ways to write the child
docs.text:
The child renders one tenant's objects. It can do that in either of two ways.

Inline gotemplate Helm chart The child Template holds spec.gotemplate: a Go template spec.helm: a reference to a published chart, plus valuesTemplate Good for A handful of objects per tenant Many objects per tenant, or logic you already have as a chart Updating it Upgrade the extension chart Publish a new tenant chart, then bump the version the child references Used by ArgoCD (one AppProject per tenant) Vault Enterprise (two dozen or more vault-config-operator CRs per tenant)

Start with an inline gotemplate. The tutorial uses one, and Real extensions shows both.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Component Version template-operator-v2 0.0.8. MTO 1.10 deploys it when the IntegrationConfig sets components.templateOperatorV2.mode: Managed. It is also available as a public chart. See Installing template-operator-v2. Kubernetes 1.33 or later tested. template-operator-v2's CRDs do not install on 1.31. On OpenShift, 4.20 matches. MTO 1.10 tested, with Tenant at tenantoperator.stakater.com/v1beta3. Helm 3, to install the chart.

An alpha API

template-operator-v2's API is templates.v2.stakater.com/v2alpha1, and its behaviour has changed between releases. For example, 0.0.8 started rendering with missingkey=error, and how objects are retained on deletion changed in 0.0.7. Pin the template-operator-v2 version you test against, write it down in your chart, and rerun your tests before you upgrade it.

docs.title: template-operator-v2
docs.text:
template-operator-v2 is Stakater's Template Operator, version 2. It is a separate operator from MTO, with its own Template and TemplateInstance kinds in the templates.v2.stakater.com group. The Templates section of these docs covers the earlier templates.stakater.com/v1alpha1 API. That is a different API, and nothing on these pages applies to it.

Template Operator essentials covers everything about template-operator-v2 that you need to write an extension.

docs.title: In this section
docs.text:
1. Template Operator essentials: the parts of template-operator-v2 that an extension uses, and how they behave.
  2. Tutorial: your first extension: build, install and test a working extension on a local cluster.
  3. Design rules: the rules that keep an extension safe in production, and how to test one.
  4. Real extensions: how the ArgoCD and Vault Enterprise extensions are built.

docs.title: Real extensions
docs.text:
Stakater's ArgoCD and Vault Enterprise extensions both use the parent and child pattern from the tutorial, but each made different choices. This page walks through those choices, with excerpts from the charts.

ArgoCD Vault Enterprise Per tenant One ArgoCD AppProject A Vault namespace, with secrets engines, login roles and policies: two dozen or more vault-config-operator CRs Downstream controller ArgoCD vault-config-operator (VCO), which writes the CRs to Vault Child written as An inline gotemplate A published Helm chart Charts One Two: a bootstrap chart installed once, and a tenant chart that template-operator-v2 pulls Who gets it Tenants that opt in (OnAnnotation by default) Every tenant with a valid name Parent reads Tenants, Namespaces, the IntegrationConfig Tenants, Namespaces Child reads Nothing: everything comes from the parent ServiceAccounts and Deployments in the tenant's namespaces

docs.title: ArgoCD
docs.text:
The ArgoCD extension gives every opted-in tenant an AppProject, scoped to that tenant's namespaces, with owner, edit and view roles. It replaces an earlier Go controller in MTO, and its whole mechanism is three template-operator-v2 objects plus RBAC.

Tenant ───────────┐
Namespace ────────┼──▶ parent TemplateInstance ──▶ one child per tenant ──▶ one AppProject per tenant
IntegrationConfig ┘

docs.title: Three inputs, three watches
docs.text:
The parent TemplateInstance reads two cluster-wide lists and one object. That is three watches however many tenants there are. A namespace event that affects one tenant rewrites only that tenant's child.

parameters:
  - name: tenants
    valueFrom:
      objectFieldRef:
        apiVersion: tenantoperator.stakater.com/v1beta3
        kind: Tenant
        jsonPath: .items
  - name: namespaces
    valueFrom:
      objectFieldRef:
        apiVersion: v1
        kind: Namespace
        jsonPath: .items
  # A GET, read shallowly at .spec. NEVER give it a defaultValue: masking a
  # failed read yields an empty privileged list, which puts privileged
  # namespaces into every tenant's destinations.
  - name: integrationConfig
    valueFrom:
      objectFieldRef:
        apiVersion: tenantoperator.stakater.com/v1beta1
        kind: IntegrationConfig
        name: tenant-operator-config
        namespace: multi-tenant-operator
        jsonPath: .spec

From the IntegrationConfig it reads only accessControl.privileged. Privileged namespaces are kept out of every tenant's destinations, and privileged groups are added to every role. If the field is absent or null, the parent refuses to render. See Fail closed.

docs.title: The parent does the cluster-wide work
docs.text:
The parent makes three passes. The first picks the opted-in tenants. The second buckets namespaces by tenant in a single pass over the Namespace list, dropping privileged namespaces. The third emits one child per tenant:

{{- range $ns := .parameters.namespaces }}
{{- $owner := dig $nsLabel "" (default dict (index $ns.metadata "labels")) }}
{{- if and $owner (hasKey $taken $owner) (or $allowCP (ne $ns.metadata.name $argoNs)) }}
{{- $isPriv := false }}
{{- range $p := $privNs }}{{- if mustRegexMatch $p $ns.metadata.name }}{{- $isPriv = true }}{{- end }}{{- end }}
{{- if not $isPriv }}{{- $_ := set $byTenant $owner (append (get $byTenant $owner | default list) $ns.metadata.name) }}{{- end }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}

The privileged-namespace check runs here, not in the child, because only the parent sees the IntegrationConfig. Everything a tenant controls is passed down as raw text.

docs.title: Per-tenant overrides, parsed in the child
docs.text:
A Tenant can override chart defaults with annotations: source repositories, resource allow and deny lists, sync windows, and whether its AppProject is deleted with it. The parent copies each annotation into a child parameter verbatim. An absent annotation inherits the chart default, and an explicit "[]" overrides it with an empty list:

{{- $wlJson := $defaultWl }}{{- if hasKey $annos $aWl }}{{- $wlJson = index $annos $aWl }}{{- end }}

The child decodes each one with mustFromJson, checks its shape field by field, and fails for that one tenant if anything is wrong. A near-miss on the purge annotation is refused rather than read as "retain":

{{- if not (has .parameters.onDeletePurge (list "true" "false")) }}
{{- fail (printf "on-delete-purge must be exactly \"true\" or \"false\", got %q" .parameters.onDeletePurge) }}
{{- end }}

docs.title: Deletion: orphan by default
docs.text:
Deleting an AppProject strands every Application that uses it. So unless purge is on, the child annotates the project to be released instead of deleted:

metadata:
  name: {{ $t | quote }}
  namespace: {{ $argoNs | quote }}
  {{- if not $purge }}
  annotations:
    templates.v2.stakater.com/deletion-policy: Orphan
  {{- end }}

docs.title: Least-privilege RBAC
docs.text:
The chart grants template-operator-v2 cluster-wide read on Tenants, Namespaces and AppProjects, but writes to AppProjects only through a RoleBinding in the ArgoCD namespace. list and watch stay cluster-wide, because teardown lists each rendered kind across the cluster. The verbs used for cleanup are granted unconditionally. Only create follows the scaffolding setting, so that turning the extension off still lets template-operator-v2 remove what it owns:

rules:
  - apiGroups: ["argoproj.io"]
    resources: ["appprojects"]
    verbs: ["get", "update", "patch", "delete"]
  {{- if ne .Values.scaffolding.mode "Never" }}
  - apiGroups: ["argoproj.io"]
    resources: ["appprojects"]
    verbs: ["create"]
  {{- end }}

Every RBAC object carries both helm.sh/resource-policy: keep and argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=false,Delete=false, so neither helm uninstall nor an ArgoCD prune can delete it before teardown is finished.

docs.title: Sync and the fields ArgoCD writes
docs.text: The Templates use sync: strict. Two fields are exempt: metadata.finalizers, which template-operator-v2 manages itself, and spec.roles[*].jwtTokens, where ArgoCD writes project tokens. Without the second exemption, argocd proj role create-token is refused by template-operator-v2's webhook. A template guard refuses strict without both exemptions at install time.

docs.title: How it is tested
docs.text: Layer Catches helm lint Chart structure Render tests, through template-operator-v2's function map Wrong AppProject content. Fixtures are discovered, not listed, so adding a file adds a test. Property tests check invariants over random clusters, and a scale test renders 1,000 tenants over about 8,000 namespaces. An equivalence test Every difference from the Go controller it replaces is deliberate and listed Admission tests with envtest Template CRs the API server would reject End-to-end on kind What template-operator-v2 and ArgoCD actually do, including paths MTO's own webhooks make untestable on a real cluster, such as a privileged namespace labelled for a tenant

docs.title: Vault Enterprise
docs.text:
The Vault Enterprise extension gives every tenant its own Vault Enterprise namespace, configured through vault-config-operator CRs. It renders configuration only; VCO writes it to Vault.

It is split into two charts:

Chart Installed Role Bootstrap Once per cluster, by hand The parent: watches Tenants, renders each tenant's Vault namespace and KV mount, and emits the child TemplateInstances. Also creates the ServiceAccount VCO logs in with. Tenant Never by hand The child: a published Helm chart that template-operator-v2 pulls and renders once per tenant. 
Tenant CRs ──► parent TemplateInstance
                 per Tenant               Namespace <tenant>, SecretEngineMount <tenant>-kv
                 per Tenant with a        TemplateInstance ...-<tenant>      → core slice
                 labelled namespace       TemplateInstance ...-<tenant>.eso  → eso slice

core slice    auth mount, a Policy and a login role per annotated ServiceAccount,
              SSO roles, and a vault-config-<sa> ConfigMap for each workload
eso slice     SecretStore and ExternalSecret objects for each workload

docs.title: A Helm chart as the child
docs.text:
With two dozen or more CRs per tenant and real logic in each, the child is a full Helm chart. The child Template points at the published chart and passes the per-tenant values through valuesTemplate. The backticks stop Helm from rendering template-operator-v2's actions when the bootstrap chart is installed:

spec:
  parameters:
    - name: tenant
      required: true
    - name: knownTenants
      value: ""
    - name: serviceAccounts
    - name: deployments
  helm:
    chart:
      repository:
        url: {{ $.Values.tenantChart.registry | quote }}
        name: {{ $.Values.tenantChart.name | quote }}
        version: {{ $.Values.tenantChart.version | quote }}
    releaseName: {{ $.Values.tenantChart.releaseName | quote }}
    version: v4
    valuesTemplate: |
      component: {{ $slice.component }}
      tenant: {{ `{{ .parameters.tenant | quote }}` }}
      knownTenants: {{ `{{ .parameters.knownTenants | quote }}` }}
      serviceAccounts: {{ `{{ .parameters.serviceAccounts | toJson }}` }}
      deployments: {{ `{{ .parameters.deployments | toJson }}` }}
      {{- $installWide | nindent 6 }}

Two consequences follow from template-operator-v2 pulling the published tenant chart:

  • Values reach the tenant chart only through the bootstrap. Editing the tenant chart's values.yaml has no effect on a cluster. The bootstrap exposes tenantValues for install-wide settings, and fails the render if one of them collides with a value it sets itself.
  • Versions must match. The bootstrap pins tenantChart.version, and a check keeps it equal to the tenant chart's own version.

docs.title: The child reads the tenant's namespaces
docs.text:
Unlike ArgoCD, the child reads the cluster too. It lists ServiceAccounts and Deployments, scoped by namespaceSelector to the tenant's labelled namespaces, and grants Vault access to each ServiceAccount that asks for it with annotations:

- name: serviceAccounts
  valueFrom:
    objectFieldRef:
      apiVersion: v1
      kind: ServiceAccount
      jsonPath: .items
      namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          stakater.com/tenant: {{ $name | quote }}

A child whose namespaceSelector matches no namespace fails parameter validation. So the parent emits children only for tenants that have at least one labelled namespace. It counts them in one pass over the Namespace list.

docs.title: Data belongs to the parent
docs.text:
A tenant's Vault namespace and KV mount hold its secrets, so they are rendered by the parent, for every valid Tenant, not by the child:

{{- range $name := $tenants }}
---
apiVersion: redhatcop.redhat.io/v1alpha1
kind: Namespace
metadata: { name: {{ $name | quote }}, namespace: {{ $cfgNs }} }
spec:
  authentication:
    {{ $auth }}
  name: {{ $name | quote }}

A child exists only while its tenant has a labelled namespace. If the Vault namespace lived in the child, deleting a tenant's last namespace would delete its Vault namespace and every secret in it. In the parent, the data lives as long as the Tenant resource. Deleting the last namespace removes the grants and keeps the secrets, and labelling a namespace again brings the grants back.

VCO has no deletion policy: deleting a Namespace CR deletes the Vault namespace. So there is a second line of defence in Vault itself. The policy VCO logs in with denies delete on namespaces and mounts. A deleted CR then stays in Terminating, and nothing is lost until an administrator decides.

docs.title: Skipping, not failing
docs.text:
The Tenant CRD does not restrict names, but a Vault namespace, a label value and the extension's dot-joined object names all do. The parent skips a tenant whose name is not a DNS label, is longer than 63 characters, or equals the shared namespace's name. It lists every skip and the reason in a ConfigMap, instead of failing the render for everyone:

{{- range $t := (default list .parameters.tenants) }}
{{- $n := toString $t.metadata.name }}
{{- if not (regexMatch "^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$" $n) }}
{{- $_ := set $skipped $n "the name is not a DNS label (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, no dots): nothing is rendered for this tenant" }}
{{- else if gt (len $n) 63 }}
...

docs.title: Errors reported where they happen
docs.text: Inside a tenant, a wrongly configured ServiceAccount does not fail the render either. It gets a ConfigMap vault-config-<sa>.error that says what is wrong, and nothing else, so one namespace's mistake does not stop the tenant's other namespaces. An unknown vault.stakater.com/ annotation is reported as an error, not ignored.

docs.title: Slices, so one missing CRD cannot break everything
docs.text: The tenant chart renders in two slices, core and eso, each from its own child Template and TemplateInstance. If the External Secrets Operator's CRDs are missing, only the .eso TemplateInstance fails, and the core Vault wiring applies regardless.

docs.title: Honest health
docs.text: A Ready child means its CRs were applied, not that VCO wrote them to Vault. The child Templates read the status VCO writes back through outputs, two fields per kind: whether the object has ever reconciled successfully, and the last error ever seen. The status cannot say more than that: VCO sets its success and failure conditions side by side, and their timestamps freeze after the first write. The extension's docs state that limit rather than implying a live health signal.

docs.title: How it is tested
docs.text:
• Render tests with fixtures and a golden render. Each guard has a check that fails when the guard is removed.
  • CRD validation of every rendered CR against a vendored copy of the VCO CRDs, through the API server's admission pipeline.
  • End-to-end on a kind lab with Vault Enterprise, VCO, Dex and Keycloak. Every assertion is made in Vault, logged in as the workload's own ServiceAccount, and every denial is paired with a matching allowed request.

docs.title: What to take from them
docs.text:
Question ArgoCD's answer Vault Enterprise's answer How much per tenant? One object, so an inline gotemplate Dozens, so a published chart What does the child need to read? Nothing beyond what the parent passes The tenant's ServiceAccounts and Deployments What must survive deletion? The AppProject, orphaned by default The data, owned by the parent and protected in Vault What can a tenant break? Only its own child, through its own annotations Only its own ServiceAccount's access, reported in an error ConfigMap

Start from the tutorial's chart, then follow whichever of these is closer to your tool.

docs.title: Template Operator essentials
docs.text:
An extension is configuration for Template Operator v2 — a parent Template + TemplateInstance that render your tenant objects. This page orients you to the parts you use and links the canonical reference; it does not repeat it. Read the Template Operator v2 docs for the full behaviour.

Both kinds live in the templates.v2.stakater.com group at v2alpha1. Use the full resource names with kubectl — templates.templates.v2.stakater.com and templateinstances.templates.v2.stakater.com — because on OpenShift the short templateinstance resolves to OpenShift's own template.openshift.io kind.

docs.title: What an extension uses, and where it's documented
docs.text:
You need For Reference Template / TemplateInstance, provider–consumer split the two objects your chart installs Overview gotemplate engine — missingkey=error, Sprig-not-Helm, mustFromJson writing the render safely Gotemplate parameters and objectFieldRef (GET vs LIST, namespaceSelector) reading Tenants, Namespaces, the IntegrationConfig Parameters outputs (from / fromAll) surfacing per-tenant health on status Outputs sync modes and ignoreFields drift protection on what you render Sync targetNamespaces where an instance may be created Target namespaces what happens to rendered objects, orphan/deletion-policy teardown behaviour Lifecycle the security model and the operator-ServiceAccount boundary scoping RBAC Security

And the patterns an extension is built on, each a worked guide:

  • The fan-out: one instance renders into many namespaces — Rendering to many namespaces.
  • Composition: a parent that renders child TemplateInstances, one per tenant — Composing TemplateInstances.
  • Testing your gotemplates the way the operator renders them — Testing Templates.

docs.title: Extension-specific notes
docs.text:
A few things matter when you are building the chart rather than using the operator:

  • Keep an extension's Templates and TemplateInstances in one namespace (the operator namespace). Then the default targetNamespaces already allows them and you never set it.
  • Parameters travel as strings. A parent passes a list or map to a child as a JSON string ({{ $v | toJson | quote }}) and the child decodes it with mustFromJson; a comma-joined empty list becomes "", which the operator rejects as unset. See Parameters.
